definition: A pattern is a reusable answer to a recurring design problem, not a copy-paste implementation.

groups.title: 01 · Creational
groups.description: Control how objects and collaborators are created.

groups.title: 02 · Structural
groups.description: Connect classes and systems without coupling everything together.

groups.title: 03 · Behavioral
groups.description: Make changing rules, operations and workflows explicit.

groups.title: 04 · Domain & data
groups.description: Make business meaning and persistence ownership explicit.

groups.title: 05 · Integration & messaging
groups.description: Move messages safely across system and ownership boundaries.

groups.title: 06 · Resilience & evolution
groups.description: Make failures contained, retries bounded and changes reversible.

groups.title: 07 · SAP implementation idioms
groups.description: Translate general design principles into ABAP, RAP and CAP safely. These are framework idioms, not extra GoF patterns.

groups.title: 08 · Testing & safe refactoring
groups.description: Prove behavior while keeping components replaceable.

patterns.name: Factory Method
patterns.problem: The caller knows a capability but not which class to instantiate.
patterns.solution: Put construction behind a method that returns an interface.
patterns.sap_example: Choose an ABAP mapping strategy per source system.
patterns.pitfall: One implementation with no likely variation.

patterns.name: Abstract Factory
patterns.problem: A family of related implementations must vary together.
patterns.solution: Expose one factory interface that creates compatible collaborators.
patterns.sap_example: Build country-specific tax and address validators as a set.
patterns.pitfall: Only one component changes independently.

patterns.name: Builder
patterns.problem: An object needs many optional values and consistency checks.
patterns.solution: Collect inputs stepwise; produce one validated result.
patterns.sap_example: Assemble a complex outbound API request with optional sections.
patterns.pitfall: A small structure can be initialized directly.

patterns.name: Prototype
patterns.problem: New objects start as copies of a configurable template.
patterns.solution: Clone a configured prototype and change explicit fields.
patterns.sap_example: Copy an immutable simulation configuration.
patterns.pitfall: Copies can accidentally share mutable references.

patterns.name: Singleton
patterns.problem: One in-process instance seems globally useful.
patterns.solution: Control construction so callers share one instance.
patterns.sap_example: Rarely suitable for a stateless ABAP helper; prefer explicit injection.
patterns.pitfall: Global mutable state breaks tests and work-process isolation.

patterns.name: Dependency Injection
patterns.problem: Construction details leak into business rules.
patterns.solution: Pass interfaces via constructor or method rather than creating them internally.
patterns.sap_example: Inject value mapping, repository and clock interfaces into a service.
patterns.pitfall: Treating a service locator as injection.

patterns.name: Lazy Initialization
patterns.problem: A dependency is expensive and may not be needed.
patterns.solution: Create or load it on first access, then reuse within a safe lifetime.
patterns.sap_example: Load optional mapping tables only for matching message types.
patterns.pitfall: Hidden first-call latency or unsafe cache scope.

patterns.name: Object Pool
patterns.problem: Acquiring reusable resources has a measurable cost.
patterns.solution: Lease bounded resources and release them reliably.
patterns.sap_example: Consider for external connection handling where platform pooling is absent.
patterns.pitfall: Pooling normal stateless ABAP objects adds complexity.

patterns.name: Parameter Object
patterns.problem: A method takes a long and unstable list of related inputs.
patterns.solution: Group a coherent set of inputs into one typed context object.
patterns.sap_example: Pass source system, org unit, message mode and trace ID together.
patterns.pitfall: Turning every unrelated input into one giant structure.

patterns.name: Static Factory
patterns.problem: A named constructor better expresses the valid object state.
patterns.solution: Provide intent-revealing creation methods that enforce invariants.
patterns.sap_example: Create a normalized customer key from validated raw input.
patterns.pitfall: A plain constructor is already sufficiently clear.

patterns.name: Adapter
patterns.problem: An existing API has the wrong interface for a client.
patterns.solution: Translate the old contract behind the interface the client expects.
patterns.sap_example: Wrap a legacy function module behind an ABAP interface.
patterns.pitfall: Copying all legacy quirks into the new contract.

patterns.name: Bridge
patterns.problem: Two independent dimensions cause a combinatorial subclass tree.
patterns.solution: Separate abstraction from implementation through composition.
patterns.sap_example: Split document processing mode from output channel.
patterns.pitfall: There is only one stable dimension.

patterns.name: Composite
patterns.problem: Individual objects and groups need the same operation.
patterns.solution: Represent leaves and groups behind one shared component interface.
patterns.sap_example: Process a hierarchy of validation rules.
patterns.pitfall: Cycles and deep recursion are not bounded.

patterns.name: Decorator
patterns.problem: Optional behavior must be added without changing the core class.
patterns.solution: Wrap a component with another component exposing the same interface.
patterns.sap_example: Add logging or timing around a mapper without changing its result.
patterns.pitfall: Wrapper order silently changes business semantics.

patterns.name: Facade
patterns.problem: Callers must coordinate too many subsystems.
patterns.solution: Expose one task-oriented operation and delegate internally.
patterns.sap_example: Offer one inbound-BP orchestration method over parsing, mapping and validation.
patterns.pitfall: Hiding important errors and transaction boundaries.

patterns.name: Flyweight
patterns.problem: Many objects repeat the same immutable state.
patterns.solution: Share immutable state separately from instance-specific state.
patterns.sap_example: Reuse metadata describing value-mapping definitions.
patterns.pitfall: Mutability or cache invalidation is uncontrolled.

patterns.name: Proxy
patterns.problem: Access to an object needs an additional boundary.
patterns.solution: Put a surrogate in front of the real object.
patterns.sap_example: Apply authorization or lazy remote lookup before a gateway call.
patterns.pitfall: An ordinary decorator is clearer and no access control is needed.

patterns.name: Anti-Corruption Layer
patterns.problem: A legacy model would contaminate the new domain model.
patterns.solution: Translate semantics at the system boundary, not throughout the core.
patterns.sap_example: Convert source-system partner roles to one canonical BP intent model.
patterns.pitfall: A shared canonical model becomes a second master.

patterns.name: Ports and Adapters
patterns.problem: Business logic depends directly on databases, SAP APIs or messaging.
patterns.solution: Define business-facing ports with infrastructure adapters.
patterns.sap_example: Switch an ABAP service between released APIs and test doubles.
patterns.pitfall: Trying to abstract away real transactional constraints.

patterns.name: Dependency Inversion
patterns.problem: High-level rules instantiate or depend on low-level utilities.
patterns.solution: Make both depend on stable abstractions.
patterns.sap_example: An ABAP handler calls an interface, not a hard-coded persistence class.
patterns.pitfall: Interfaces without a genuine ownership boundary.

patterns.name: Gateway
patterns.problem: External service details leak into many callers.
patterns.solution: Centralize one external system's communication contract.
patterns.sap_example: Encapsulate BP read API calls and remote errors.
patterns.pitfall: A gateway becomes an unbounded god class.

patterns.name: Wrapper
patterns.problem: A risky existing component cannot be changed yet.
patterns.solution: Contain it behind a narrow safe interface.
patterns.sap_example: Protect a classic BAPI until a released interface is available.
patterns.pitfall: The wrapper is used as an excuse to expand unreleased dependencies.

patterns.name: Front Controller
patterns.problem: Multiple entry points duplicate authorization and dispatch rules.
patterns.solution: Route requests through one application entry point.
patterns.sap_example: Centralize selection of inbound message processing commands.
patterns.pitfall: A framework already provides this boundary.

patterns.name: Backend for Frontend
patterns.problem: Different consumers need distinct APIs and shapes.
patterns.solution: Provide consumer-oriented facades over stable domain services.
patterns.sap_example: Offer a mobile-facing CAP service separately from the Fiori UI contract.
patterns.pitfall: Duplicating business ownership in every frontend.

patterns.name: Layered Architecture
patterns.problem: UI, business rules and persistence are tangled together.
patterns.solution: Split presentation, application/domain and infrastructure responsibilities.
patterns.sap_example: Keep RAP behavior handler thin and delegate reusable rules.
patterns.pitfall: Layers only forward calls without distinct responsibility.

patterns.name: Strategy
patterns.problem: A growing CASE statement chooses one of many algorithms.
patterns.solution: Define one algorithm interface and select a concrete strategy.
patterns.sap_example: Apply org-specific BP enrichment or validation.
patterns.pitfall: Two branches are simple and unlikely to grow.

patterns.name: Specification
patterns.problem: Business eligibility rules need reuse and composition.
patterns.solution: Represent a rule as a predicate that can be combined with other predicates.
patterns.sap_example: Check whether a BP is eligible for replication.
patterns.pitfall: The rule needs ordered side effects rather than a true or false answer.

patterns.name: Command
patterns.problem: Operations need a common contract, audit or deferred execution.
patterns.solution: Represent one requested operation as an object with execute behavior.
patterns.sap_example: Model create, change and skip actions for inbound IDoc handling.
patterns.pitfall: A direct method call is sufficient.

patterns.name: Chain of Responsibility
patterns.problem: Several handlers may resolve the same request, with precedence.
patterns.solution: Pass a request along an explicit chain until handled.
patterns.sap_example: Try specific mapping exception then generic org mapping.
patterns.pitfall: The business rule requires all handlers to run.

patterns.name: State
patterns.problem: Behavior changes according to a valid lifecycle state.
patterns.solution: Represent transitions explicitly rather than scattering status checks.
patterns.sap_example: Control approval, locked and ready-to-replicate states.
patterns.pitfall: Status is only read, not behavior-changing.

patterns.name: Template Method
patterns.problem: Multiple workflows share stable steps but vary at chosen points.
patterns.solution: Place algorithm skeleton in a base class with extension hooks.
patterns.sap_example: Reuse common extract-map-validate-send steps across interfaces.
patterns.pitfall: Composition would avoid inheritance coupling.

patterns.name: Observer
patterns.problem: Several consumers react to a state change.
patterns.solution: Publish a notification and register independent listeners.
patterns.sap_example: Notify audit and metrics components after an application event.
patterns.pitfall: A durable integration contract is required instead.

patterns.name: Mediator
patterns.problem: Peer objects know too much about one another.
patterns.solution: Centralize coordination in a mediator.
patterns.sap_example: Coordinate rule evaluation and response assembly.
patterns.pitfall: The mediator becomes a god object.

patterns.name: Iterator
patterns.problem: Callers should traverse a collection without knowing its representation.
patterns.solution: Expose a traversal contract.
patterns.sap_example: Stream through a large derived business list safely.
patterns.pitfall: Ordinary ABAP table LOOP is clear enough.

patterns.name: Visitor
patterns.problem: Different operations run over a stable hierarchy of types.
patterns.solution: Put operations in visitors without changing element classes.
patterns.sap_example: Render or validate a stable tree of rule nodes.
patterns.pitfall: Element types change frequently.

patterns.name: Memento
patterns.problem: A state snapshot is needed to restore a previous state.
patterns.solution: Capture and restore authorized state without exposing internals.
patterns.sap_example: Support UI undo in a non-transactional editor.
patterns.pitfall: Using it as a database rollback replacement.

patterns.name: Interpreter
patterns.problem: A simple bounded grammar must execute rules.
patterns.solution: Represent grammar expressions as an evaluable tree.
patterns.sap_example: Evaluate a controlled expression language for routing rules.
patterns.pitfall: A full arbitrary scripting engine is unnecessary or unsafe.

patterns.name: Null Object
patterns.problem: Clients repeatedly branch on missing optional behavior.
patterns.solution: Supply an intentional no-op implementation of an interface.
patterns.sap_example: Use a no-op telemetry provider in test scenarios.
patterns.pitfall: Absence must cause an error.

patterns.name: Policy Object
patterns.problem: The same decision varies by configurable business policy.
patterns.solution: Encapsulate decision rules behind a policy interface.
patterns.sap_example: Choose which customer fields may be updated by source system.
patterns.pitfall: A policy secretly executes persistence changes.

patterns.name: Rule Engine
patterns.problem: Rules change often and non-developers need to govern them.
patterns.solution: Externalize versioned conditions into a governed rule model.
patterns.sap_example: Drive org-specific mapping rules from controlled configuration.
patterns.pitfall: Hard-to-debug runtime DSL replaces three stable conditions.

patterns.name: Pipeline
patterns.problem: A process consists of independently testable ordered stages.
patterns.solution: Chain explicit stages with defined input and output contracts.
patterns.sap_example: Parse, normalize, validate and publish an inbound record.
patterns.pitfall: Stage ordering and failure behavior are undefined.

patterns.name: Guard Clause
patterns.problem: Nested conditions hide the real work.
patterns.solution: Reject invalid or irrelevant cases early.
patterns.sap_example: Skip deleted or wait-mode BP records before enrichment.
patterns.pitfall: An early return bypasses required cleanup.

patterns.name: Double Dispatch
patterns.problem: Behavior depends on two runtime types.
patterns.solution: Select behavior using two dynamic dispatch steps.
patterns.sap_example: Apply node-type and operation-type handling in a rule tree.
patterns.pitfall: A small lookup table is simpler.

patterns.name: Predicate
patterns.problem: A business selection condition needs a clear name.
patterns.solution: Express the check as a side-effect-free true/false function.
patterns.sap_example: Determine whether an email record meets a selection rule.
patterns.pitfall: It reads external mutable state unpredictably.

patterns.name: Composite Specification
patterns.problem: Simple eligibility rules must be joined flexibly.
patterns.solution: Compose AND, OR and NOT specifications without side effects.
patterns.sap_example: Combine active BP, permitted source and target-org criteria.
patterns.pitfall: Rule order matters or rules mutate data.

patterns.name: Command Handler
patterns.problem: Request representation and execution mechanics need separation.
patterns.solution: Map command type to an independently testable handler.
patterns.sap_example: Dispatch normalized IDoc operations to classes.
patterns.pitfall: A command bus adds indirection with no benefit.

patterns.name: Policy Registry
patterns.problem: Multiple policies are chosen by keys at runtime.
patterns.solution: Look up a policy through a controlled registry/factory.
patterns.sap_example: Select sales-org logic with fallback precedence.
patterns.pitfall: Unknown keys silently fall back to the wrong behavior.

patterns.name: Explicit State Machine
patterns.problem: Transition order and allowed actions matter more than UI flags.
patterns.solution: Store an explicit state plus allowed events and guards.
patterns.sap_example: Enforce request lifecycle from prepared to activated.
patterns.pitfall: States are only labels without real transitions.

patterns.name: Entity
patterns.problem: Identity matters beyond the current field values.
patterns.solution: Model identity and lifecycle explicitly.
patterns.sap_example: Represent a business partner independently of a display name.
patterns.pitfall: Treating identical field values as identical entities.

patterns.name: Value Object
patterns.problem: Small business concepts lack a reliable equality rule.
patterns.solution: Use immutable values with validation and value equality.
patterns.sap_example: A normalized sales organization key or tax identifier.
patterns.pitfall: Mutable references undermine equality.

patterns.name: Aggregate
patterns.problem: Related entities need one consistency boundary.
patterns.solution: Choose an aggregate root that enforces invariants.
patterns.sap_example: Group a custom approval request and its entries.
patterns.pitfall: One aggregate includes an entire ERP landscape.

patterns.name: Aggregate Root
patterns.problem: External callers bypass invariants on related objects.
patterns.solution: Permit state changes through the consistency owner.
patterns.sap_example: Update a custom request via its root operation.
patterns.pitfall: A root is only a bag of CRUD methods.

patterns.name: Domain Service
patterns.problem: A domain operation does not belong naturally to one entity.
patterns.solution: Place the operation in an explicit domain service.
patterns.sap_example: Apply eligibility calculation across partner and sales data.
patterns.pitfall: Infrastructure calls dominate the purported domain service.

patterns.name: Application Service
patterns.problem: Consumers duplicate orchestration and transaction flow.
patterns.solution: Provide use-case methods that coordinate domain collaborators.
patterns.sap_example: Run customer activation checks and call a released write API.
patterns.pitfall: Business rules stay hidden inside controller logic.

patterns.name: Repository
patterns.problem: Domain logic depends on how entities are loaded and saved.
patterns.solution: Expose collection-like access behind a persistence interface.
patterns.sap_example: Read custom mapping policies without SQL in every rule.
patterns.pitfall: Direct table access bypasses RAP BO behavior and authorization.

patterns.name: Unit of Work
patterns.problem: Several in-memory changes need coordinated persistence.
patterns.solution: Track a transactional change set and commit it once.
patterns.sap_example: Coordinate one permitted custom transaction in classic ABAP.
patterns.pitfall: Implementing custom COMMIT inside RAP handler methods.

patterns.name: Identity Map
patterns.problem: The same entity is loaded repeatedly in one operation.
patterns.solution: Keep one identity-keyed in-process instance per logical unit.
patterns.sap_example: Avoid duplicate reads during one mass-processing package.
patterns.pitfall: Caching across users or changes without invalidation.

patterns.name: Data Mapper
patterns.problem: Domain structures should not depend on database tables.
patterns.solution: Translate between persistence records and domain values.
patterns.sap_example: Map a legacy customer record into a canonical object.
patterns.pitfall: Duplicated with standard CDS projections for no reason.

patterns.name: Data Transfer Object
patterns.problem: An interface should not leak internal domain objects.
patterns.solution: Define a stable, minimal transport structure.
patterns.sap_example: Use a normalized inbound BP payload between stages.
patterns.pitfall: One DTO becomes a universal model for all interfaces.

patterns.name: Transaction Script
patterns.problem: Simple independent business operations need minimal machinery.
patterns.solution: Implement one explicit procedure per use case.
patterns.sap_example: Run a single controlled batch correction.
patterns.pitfall: Branch-heavy and duplicated rules signal a domain model need.

patterns.name: Domain Event
patterns.problem: Other components need to know that a business fact occurred.
patterns.solution: Publish immutable facts after an authorized state change.
patterns.sap_example: Notify that custom onboarding approval completed.
patterns.pitfall: Confusing an event with a mutable command.

patterns.name: Event Sourcing
patterns.problem: A system must derive state from an authoritative event history.
patterns.solution: Store and replay versioned domain events.
patterns.sap_example: Audit-heavy custom workflow with explicit replay semantics.
patterns.pitfall: Ordinary change logs solve the need with less complexity.

patterns.name: CQRS
patterns.problem: Reads and writes need different optimized models.
patterns.solution: Separate command-side invariants from read projections.
patterns.sap_example: Provide a reporting CDS view alongside controlled write operations.
patterns.pitfall: One CRUD app does not need two models.

patterns.name: Service Layer
patterns.problem: Multiple clients need one use-case boundary.
patterns.solution: Expose operations instead of raw persistence internals.
patterns.sap_example: Provide customer request processing service to jobs and UI.
patterns.pitfall: Pass-through methods add noise.

patterns.name: Active Record
patterns.problem: Data and simple persistence behavior travel together.
patterns.solution: Let one record-like object manage its own persistence.
patterns.sap_example: Small custom admin object in a non-RAP context.
patterns.pitfall: It couples domain logic and storage in complex solutions.

patterns.name: Table Data Gateway
patterns.problem: Many operations target one table without rich domain rules.
patterns.solution: Centralize SQL for a given table behind a gateway.
patterns.sap_example: Read a custom customizing table through a narrow access class.
patterns.pitfall: Gateways bypass released SAP APIs or RAP contracts.

patterns.name: Domain Primitive
patterns.problem: An ordinary primitive hides critical validation.
patterns.solution: Use a named constrained type for a business concept.
patterns.sap_example: Represent a non-empty country code or validated e-mail.
patterns.pitfall: Type wrappers multiply without real invariants.

patterns.name: Mapping Registry
patterns.problem: Mapping selection is scattered over business logic.
patterns.solution: Maintain typed, versioned mapping entries and lookup precedence.
patterns.sap_example: Resolve source-to-target sales org mappings centrally.
patterns.pitfall: Configuration changes without governance or audit.

patterns.name: Message Translator
patterns.problem: Connected systems speak different data shapes.
patterns.solution: Translate between owned message contracts at the boundary.
patterns.sap_example: Convert inbound customer segments into canonical intent.
patterns.pitfall: Translator also performs business posting.

patterns.name: Content-Based Router
patterns.problem: Destination depends on message content.
patterns.solution: Choose an endpoint using explicit content predicates.
patterns.sap_example: Route a message according to sending system or business object.
patterns.pitfall: Complex rules are hidden in middleware scripts.

patterns.name: Message Filter
patterns.problem: Irrelevant messages should not reach the processor.
patterns.solution: Reject non-matching messages early and visibly.
patterns.sap_example: Ignore records marked wait or not in replication scope.
patterns.pitfall: Silently dropping messages without traceability.

patterns.name: Splitter
patterns.problem: One input contains independently processable items.
patterns.solution: Create separate tracked messages for each unit.
patterns.sap_example: Split a bulk customer payload into per-BP units.
patterns.pitfall: Splitting breaks required all-or-nothing consistency.

patterns.name: Aggregator
patterns.problem: Several related messages must produce one result.
patterns.solution: Collect parts by correlation key and completion rule.
patterns.sap_example: Reconcile acknowledgements for a replicated customer package.
patterns.pitfall: No timeout, partial-failure or late-message policy.

patterns.name: Resequencer
patterns.problem: Message order changes during asynchronous delivery.
patterns.solution: Buffer and emit by sequence with finite retention.
patterns.sap_example: Apply versioned BP updates in source order.
patterns.pitfall: Unlimited buffering creates operational deadlocks.

patterns.name: Scatter-Gather
patterns.problem: Multiple recipients can contribute to one decision.
patterns.solution: Fan out requests then combine responses with timeout policy.
patterns.sap_example: Check availability across several services.
patterns.pitfall: Synchronous fan-out stalls a critical SAP process.

patterns.name: Routing Slip
patterns.problem: Each message carries an authorized processing route.
patterns.solution: Execute a list of named steps in validated order.
patterns.sap_example: Run an approved enrichment sequence by scenario.
patterns.pitfall: Caller-supplied arbitrary execution names.

patterns.name: Recipient List
patterns.problem: Recipients vary per request.
patterns.solution: Resolve a controlled list of destinations dynamically.
patterns.sap_example: Send one business event to configured subscribers.
patterns.pitfall: All destinations are hard-coded in a single processor.

patterns.name: Pipes and Filters
patterns.problem: Transformation stages are too tightly coupled.
patterns.solution: Chain small reusable filters through explicit channels.
patterns.sap_example: Normalize, enrich and validate integration payloads.
patterns.pitfall: Failures lose original input and trace IDs.

patterns.name: Correlation Identifier
patterns.problem: Replies cannot be tied reliably to requests.
patterns.solution: Include an immutable correlation key end to end.
patterns.sap_example: Join DRFOUT message attempts to target acknowledgement.
patterns.pitfall: A business key alone is not unique per attempt.

patterns.name: Envelope Wrapper
patterns.problem: Cross-cutting transport metadata contaminates payload.
patterns.solution: Wrap payload with trace, schema and routing metadata.
patterns.sap_example: Carry source-system and logical-message identity with BP data.
patterns.pitfall: Envelope format changes without versioning.

patterns.name: Canonical Data Model
patterns.problem: Many pairwise integrations need shared vocabulary.
patterns.solution: Define a deliberately scoped canonical contract.
patterns.sap_example: Normalize org and partner-role semantics between systems.
patterns.pitfall: Canonical model becomes a global ungoverned database.

patterns.name: Content Enricher
patterns.problem: A message lacks fields needed downstream.
patterns.solution: Add missing fields through defined, observable lookups.
patterns.sap_example: Enrich customer routing keys from a permitted source.
patterns.pitfall: Guessing missing values from unrelated records.

patterns.name: Content Filter
patterns.problem: Consumers should receive only required data.
patterns.solution: Remove unnecessary fields while preserving context.
patterns.sap_example: Send a reduced BP event to a subscriber.
patterns.pitfall: Removing fields required for semantic consistency.

patterns.name: Claim Check
patterns.problem: Payload is too large to carry across channels.
patterns.solution: Store payload durably and send a secure retrieval token.
patterns.sap_example: Transfer large attachment references instead of bytes.
patterns.pitfall: Retention or authorization for claim check is unclear.

patterns.name: Request-Reply
patterns.problem: The caller needs a correlated response.
patterns.solution: Define response contract, timeout and error mapping.
patterns.sap_example: Read shipping information from a synchronous API.
patterns.pitfall: A long-running workflow is forced to block.

patterns.name: Publish-Subscribe
patterns.problem: Independent consumers need the same fact.
patterns.solution: Publish an event to subscribed receivers.
patterns.sap_example: Fan out a customer-created event to audit and analytics.
patterns.pitfall: Consumers assume exactly-once delivery.

patterns.name: Competing Consumers
patterns.problem: Backlog requires parallel workers.
patterns.solution: Run multiple consumers against one durable queue.
patterns.sap_example: Scale independent outbound enrichment jobs.
patterns.pitfall: Processing order is mandatory per business key.

patterns.name: Dead Letter Channel
patterns.problem: Repeatedly failing messages block normal traffic.
patterns.solution: Move exhausted messages to a monitored exception channel.
patterns.sap_example: Quarantine an invalid mapping payload for investigation.
patterns.pitfall: Nobody owns reprocessing and alerts.

patterns.name: Idempotent Consumer
patterns.problem: Retries and duplicates may apply the same change twice.
patterns.solution: Identify a logical message and suppress duplicate effects.
patterns.sap_example: Handle repeated inbound IDoc deliveries safely.
patterns.pitfall: Every resend is assumed to be the same business state.

patterns.name: Transactional Outbox
patterns.problem: State commit and event publication can diverge.
patterns.solution: Persist event intent in the same authorized transaction; publish later.
patterns.sap_example: Emit custom application event after request activation.
patterns.pitfall: Trying to create your own SAP standard save protocol.

patterns.name: Inbox Pattern
patterns.problem: Duplicate or reordered incoming messages need durable tracking.
patterns.solution: Record message receipt, status and processing outcome.
patterns.sap_example: Protect BP update ingress from repeated message IDs.
patterns.pitfall: Idempotency key scope is not defined.

patterns.name: Saga
patterns.problem: A business process spans independent transactions.
patterns.solution: Coordinate local steps with explicit compensations.
patterns.sap_example: Orchestrate custom onboarding across external services.
patterns.pitfall: Pretending compensations are database rollback.

patterns.name: Transactional Client
patterns.problem: Message consumption and local state update need consistency.
patterns.solution: Coordinate acknowledgement with the supported transaction model.
patterns.sap_example: Consume a custom queue and persist a receipt atomically where supported.
patterns.pitfall: Assuming end-to-end distributed ACID transactions.

patterns.name: Polling Consumer
patterns.problem: No callback exists for available work.
patterns.solution: Poll with a safe interval, cursor and ownership model.
patterns.sap_example: Consume pending outbound integration tasks.
patterns.pitfall: Hot polling or duplicates under parallel runners.

patterns.name: Event-Driven Consumer
patterns.problem: Work should start when a message arrives.
patterns.solution: Invoke a bounded handler from the messaging runtime.
patterns.sap_example: React to a published customer lifecycle event.
patterns.pitfall: Handler performs long synchronous operations.

patterns.name: Message History
patterns.problem: Incident analysis needs to know where a message traveled.
patterns.solution: Capture a minimal end-to-end processing trail.
patterns.sap_example: Track logical BP replication steps and target response.
patterns.pitfall: Logging confidential payloads unnecessarily.

patterns.name: Wire Tap
patterns.problem: Diagnostics need a copy of the flow without changing it.
patterns.solution: Send a controlled observability copy to a secure monitor.
patterns.sap_example: Capture test flow metadata for replay diagnosis.
patterns.pitfall: A tap leaks payloads or becomes part of business logic.

patterns.name: Message Store
patterns.problem: Operations need durable searchable message records.
patterns.solution: Persist selected message metadata and lifecycle states.
patterns.sap_example: Inspect which customer delivery failed or was retried.
patterns.pitfall: Treating the store as a new business source of truth.

patterns.name: Message Broker
patterns.problem: Publishers and consumers should not know each other directly.
patterns.solution: Use managed routing to bridge endpoints.
patterns.sap_example: Integrate SAP event publishers with authorized consumers.
patterns.pitfall: Broker policies are a hidden source of business rules.

patterns.name: Normalizer
patterns.problem: Different inbound formats represent the same business meaning.
patterns.solution: Translate variants into one controlled representation.
patterns.sap_example: Normalize customer updates received by API and IDoc.
patterns.pitfall: Normalization erases important origin semantics.

patterns.name: Retry with Backoff
patterns.problem: Transient failures can clear without intervention.
patterns.solution: Retry only recoverable operations with delay, jitter and limits.
patterns.sap_example: Retry HTTP 503 when an external mapping API is unavailable.
patterns.pitfall: Retrying a non-idempotent write blindly.

patterns.name: Circuit Breaker
patterns.problem: Repeated remote failures overload a system.
patterns.solution: Stop calls temporarily after a failure threshold.
patterns.sap_example: Protect inbound processing from a failing remote enrichment API.
patterns.pitfall: One temporary fault opens the breaker forever.

patterns.name: Bulkhead
patterns.problem: One overloaded integration exhausts shared capacity.
patterns.solution: Isolate workload limits by destination or function.
patterns.sap_example: Prevent slow third-party calls starving BP replication workers.
patterns.pitfall: Isolation is only a label with no resource boundary.

patterns.name: Timeout
patterns.problem: External operations can wait indefinitely.
patterns.solution: Define explicit maximum wait and timeout handling.
patterns.sap_example: Bound synchronous customer validation API calls.
patterns.pitfall: The timeout silently leaves an unknown write outcome.

patterns.name: Rate Limiting
patterns.problem: Bursts exceed remote API or SAP processing capacity.
patterns.solution: Apply governed request quotas and feedback.
patterns.sap_example: Throttle mass API replication to target constraints.
patterns.pitfall: Dropping business-critical requests instead of queueing.

patterns.name: Queue-Based Load Leveling
patterns.problem: Producer spikes overwhelm a consumer.
patterns.solution: Buffer work in a durable queue and scale consumers safely.
patterns.sap_example: Process large customer updates asynchronously.
patterns.pitfall: Backlog has no monitoring or age SLA.

patterns.name: Backpressure
patterns.problem: Downstream throughput is lower than the upstream load.
patterns.solution: Signal or enforce bounded production rates.
patterns.sap_example: Slow inbound batch feed when the target is overloaded.
patterns.pitfall: Unlimited buffering masquerades as backpressure.

patterns.name: Cache-Aside
patterns.problem: Repeated reads are expensive but not all need freshness.
patterns.solution: Read cache first; load and populate on miss.
patterns.sap_example: Cache stable customizing within a defined lifetime.
patterns.pitfall: Cache makes mutable master data stale.

patterns.name: Feature Flag
patterns.problem: New behavior must be switched independently from deployment.
patterns.solution: Gate the feature behind a reversible, governed toggle.
patterns.sap_example: Enable a new mapping rule for one source system.
patterns.pitfall: Flags never expire and obscure production logic.

patterns.name: Branch by Abstraction
patterns.problem: A large change cannot be deployed in one step.
patterns.solution: Introduce an interface and replace implementations incrementally.
patterns.sap_example: Migrate from classic BP adapter to a released API adapter.
patterns.pitfall: Two implementations remain indefinitely.

patterns.name: Strangler Fig
patterns.problem: Legacy functionality must be replaced gradually.
patterns.solution: Route specific capabilities to the new system over time.
patterns.sap_example: Move selected custom interface operations to a side-by-side service.
patterns.pitfall: Two systems both become authoritative.

patterns.name: Blue-Green Deployment
patterns.problem: Rollback must not require rebuilding an old artifact.
patterns.solution: Keep two deployable versions and switch traffic safely.
patterns.sap_example: Release a BTP CAP extension with a controlled cutover.
patterns.pitfall: Database and API compatibility are ignored.

patterns.name: Canary Release
patterns.problem: Risk of a change is unknown at full traffic.
patterns.solution: Expose a small safe slice and monitor outcomes.
patterns.sap_example: Route a limited allowed group to new enrichment logic.
patterns.pitfall: Rollout cannot be isolated by consumer or business key.

patterns.name: Compensating Transaction
patterns.problem: A completed distributed step cannot be physically rolled back.
patterns.solution: Define a business reversal with an auditable outcome.
patterns.sap_example: Reverse an external reservation after failed approval.
patterns.pitfall: Compensation is treated as guaranteed rollback.

patterns.name: Health Endpoint Monitoring
patterns.problem: Infrastructure is up but a dependency may be unhealthy.
patterns.solution: Expose scoped readiness checks with clear failure thresholds.
patterns.sap_example: Monitor CAP service readiness and integration connectivity.
patterns.pitfall: Probe writes business data or exposes credentials.

patterns.name: Leader Election
patterns.problem: Exactly one coordinator should own a scheduled task.
patterns.solution: Elect a lease-based owner with expiration and fencing.
patterns.sap_example: Coordinate a custom singleton reconciliation worker.
patterns.pitfall: Assuming SAP work processes share in-memory state.

patterns.name: Checkpointing
patterns.problem: Long operations must resume after interruption.
patterns.solution: Persist a stable cursor or completed unit boundary.
patterns.sap_example: Resume mass BP validation from last confirmed package.
patterns.pitfall: A cursor skips rows that changed during processing.

patterns.name: Released API Boundary
patterns.problem: Custom logic reaches into unstable SAP internals.
patterns.solution: Depend on released interfaces supported in the target context.
patterns.sap_example: Access business objects through released APIs or EML when appropriate.
patterns.pitfall: A classic internal table is assumed clean-core safe.

patterns.name: Thin RAP Handler
patterns.problem: Behavior pool methods grow into untestable procedures.
patterns.solution: Delegate pure rules and coordination to focused service classes.
patterns.sap_example: Call a specification service from a RAP validation.
patterns.pitfall: Delegation hides prohibited transaction operations.

patterns.name: RAP Managed BO
patterns.problem: Standard persistence behavior should be framework-owned.
patterns.solution: Use managed behavior where its transactional model fits.
patterns.sap_example: Create a custom application object with validation and action.
patterns.pitfall: Managed mode is chosen for existing complex legacy persistence.

patterns.name: RAP Unmanaged BO
patterns.problem: Existing transactional logic must remain the write owner.
patterns.solution: Implement required RAP behavior contracts explicitly.
patterns.sap_example: Expose a custom legacy document safely via RAP.
patterns.pitfall: Assuming unmanaged supports every managed trigger.

patterns.name: RAP Draft Handling
patterns.problem: Interactive edits need safe unfinished state.
patterns.solution: Use framework draft behavior instead of custom shadow tables.
patterns.sap_example: Support review before activating a custom request.
patterns.pitfall: Draft is mistaken for an approval workflow.

patterns.name: RAP Validation
patterns.problem: A business object must reject inconsistent state.
patterns.solution: Validate at supported trigger points and populate FAILED/REPORTED.
patterns.sap_example: Reject a custom request missing a mandatory key.
patterns.pitfall: Trying to MODIFY entities in a validation.

patterns.name: RAP Determination
patterns.problem: A value must be derived when tracked inputs change.
patterns.solution: Define a framework determination with idempotent logic.
patterns.sap_example: Derive an optional attribute from stable request fields.
patterns.pitfall: Relying on determination order.

patterns.name: RAP Action
patterns.problem: A business operation is richer than CRUD.
patterns.solution: Expose the operation as a typed behavior action.
patterns.sap_example: Offer an approve operation on a custom object.
patterns.pitfall: Putting the action's semantics into the UI only.

patterns.name: RAP Feature Control
patterns.problem: Allowed actions vary by instance state.
patterns.solution: Publish feature availability through RAP control.
patterns.sap_example: Disable approval after completion.
patterns.pitfall: Enforcing security only in feature control.

patterns.name: RAP Authorization
patterns.problem: Object-level operations need explicit permissions.
patterns.solution: Use RAP authorization control plus appropriate backend checks.
patterns.sap_example: Restrict changes to an authorized owner role.
patterns.pitfall: UI hiding is mistaken for authorization.

patterns.name: EML Consumer Boundary
patterns.problem: Internal code bypasses the behavior contract with SQL writes.
patterns.solution: Consume behavior through typed EML where supported.
patterns.sap_example: Update a custom RAP BO from an ABAP orchestrator.
patterns.pitfall: Manual COMMIT inside a RAP behavior handler.

patterns.name: CDS Projection
patterns.problem: Consumers need a constrained public view of domain data.
patterns.solution: Expose purpose-built CDS projections and service contracts.
patterns.sap_example: Provide a read-only consumer-facing BP summary.
patterns.pitfall: Projections hide missing authorization requirements.

patterns.name: BAdI as Strategy
patterns.problem: SAP extension point calls business-specific custom logic.
patterns.solution: Implement a small BAdI adapter delegating to strategies.
patterns.sap_example: Select a mapping policy within a permitted BAdI.
patterns.pitfall: A BAdI is used for destructive direct-table updates.

patterns.name: Configuration-Driven Policy
patterns.problem: Changes to org-level rules should not require code branches.
patterns.solution: Load versioned customizing and select a typed rule implementation.
patterns.sap_example: Configure which customer attributes may be updated per org.
patterns.pitfall: Configuration allows arbitrary executable behavior.

patterns.name: CAP Before Handler
patterns.problem: Request fields require application checks before generic handling.
patterns.solution: Register a before handler for validation and normalization.
patterns.sap_example: Validate custom request fields in CAP.
patterns.pitfall: Mutating unrelated state on every request.

patterns.name: CAP On Handler
patterns.problem: A custom event requires operation ownership.
patterns.solution: Implement an explicit on handler for a custom action.
patterns.sap_example: Handle a submitForReview CAP action.
patterns.pitfall: Overriding generic CRUD without business need.

patterns.name: CAP After Handler
patterns.problem: Response needs derived or consumer-specific enrichment.
patterns.solution: Enrich returned data after generic handling.
patterns.sap_example: Add calculated display metadata to CAP reads.
patterns.pitfall: Confusing output decoration with durable persistence.

patterns.name: Side-by-Side Extension
patterns.problem: A custom capability should not alter S/4 core internals.
patterns.solution: Build a separate BTP service consuming released APIs/events.
patterns.sap_example: Run an external enrichment and review application.
patterns.pitfall: Duplicating S/4 business data ownership.

patterns.name: IDoc Normalization Boundary
patterns.problem: Segment-level rules scatter across inbound processing.
patterns.solution: Normalize segments and function codes before selecting command.
patterns.sap_example: Convert generic inbound record into create/change/skip intent.
patterns.pitfall: Using MSGFN as a substitute for business key validation.

patterns.name: Deterministic Mapping Lookup
patterns.problem: Org-dependent mapping logic is inconsistent across call sites.
patterns.solution: Resolve scoped mapping with explicit precedence and missing-key handling.
patterns.sap_example: Look up target sales organization in governed customizing.
patterns.pitfall: A failed lookup silently returns a default.

patterns.name: Test Double
patterns.problem: A dependency is too slow, expensive or unpredictable in tests.
patterns.solution: Replace it with a controlled implementation of its interface.
patterns.sap_example: Test ABAP mapping without calling RFC or persistence.
patterns.pitfall: The double pretends to prove full integration.

patterns.name: Stub
patterns.problem: The subject needs canned input from a collaborator.
patterns.solution: Return deterministic values from an injected collaborator.
patterns.sap_example: Make a value-mapping service return a fixed sales org.
patterns.pitfall: Tests assert interaction counts instead of output.

patterns.name: Mock
patterns.problem: A required interaction with a collaborator must be verified.
patterns.solution: Set expectations on observable calls.
patterns.sap_example: Assert a gateway was called once with a valid command.
patterns.pitfall: Every internal call becomes an implementation-coupled assertion.

patterns.name: Fake
patterns.problem: A lightweight working substitute accelerates tests.
patterns.solution: Use an in-memory implementation of a repository.
patterns.sap_example: Store mapping rules in memory during ABAP Unit.
patterns.pitfall: A fake hides unique constraints and concurrency.

patterns.name: Spy
patterns.problem: An interaction log is needed after execution.
patterns.solution: Record calls made to a test collaborator.
patterns.sap_example: Inspect transmitted commands and trace identifiers.
patterns.pitfall: The spy exposes private implementation details unnecessarily.

patterns.name: Test Data Builder
patterns.problem: Complex input fixtures obscure test intent.
patterns.solution: Provide focused defaults with readable overrides.
patterns.sap_example: Create synthetic BP inputs with only relevant exceptions.
patterns.pitfall: Tests rely on many hidden defaults.

patterns.name: Characterization Test
patterns.problem: Legacy behavior must be captured before refactoring.
patterns.solution: Write tests that document current observable behavior.
patterns.sap_example: Lock down mapping precedence before replacing a CASE.
patterns.pitfall: Documenting a bug as an untouchable requirement.

patterns.name: Golden Master
patterns.problem: Outputs are large but stable enough for comparison.
patterns.solution: Compare approved output snapshots after normalization.
patterns.sap_example: Detect unexpected changes in a synthetic IDoc transformation.
patterns.pitfall: Volatile fields cause noisy failures.

patterns.name: Contract Test
patterns.problem: Two components must agree on an integration contract.
patterns.solution: Validate requests and responses against a shared schema.
patterns.sap_example: Test an outbound CAP service payload version.
patterns.pitfall: Both sides implement the same wrong assumptions.

patterns.name: Consumer-Driven Contract
patterns.problem: Provider changes risk breaking specific consumers.
patterns.solution: Let consumers express verified expectations for provider behavior.
patterns.sap_example: Protect a BTP integration from unexpected API changes.
patterns.pitfall: A contract test replaces authorization and load tests.

patterns.name: Property-Based Test
patterns.problem: Many input combinations are hard to enumerate.
patterns.solution: Generate cases around invariants, not specific examples.
patterns.sap_example: Check mapping normalization is idempotent for arbitrary valid keys.
patterns.pitfall: Generator omits important business constraints.

patterns.name: Mutation Testing
patterns.problem: Tests pass but may not detect defective changes.
patterns.solution: Alter operators intentionally and observe failing tests.
patterns.sap_example: Challenge a customer eligibility predicate.
patterns.pitfall: Mutation score is mistaken for product correctness.

patterns.name: Dependency Seam
patterns.problem: Hard-coded collaborators prevent isolated changes.
patterns.solution: Add one controlled injection point with minimal behavior change.
patterns.sap_example: Extract a function-module call behind an ABAP interface.
patterns.pitfall: The seam becomes permanent unowned duplication.

patterns.name: Approval Test
patterns.problem: Human-readable output needs reviewed expected results.
patterns.solution: Review and store a canonical expected artifact.
patterns.sap_example: Approve a synthetic reconciliation report output.
patterns.pitfall: Approvals update automatically after every change.

patterns.name: Architecture Fitness Function
patterns.problem: Architectural rules must survive ongoing changes.
patterns.solution: Enforce boundaries through automated static checks.
patterns.sap_example: Check released APIs, dependency direction and forbidden commits.
patterns.pitfall: The check merely counts files instead of verifying risk.

patterns.name: Hexagonal Test
patterns.problem: Business logic must work without external SAP services.
patterns.solution: Exercise an inbound port using test adapters.
patterns.sap_example: Test the BP eligibility service without DB and RFC.
patterns.pitfall: Ignoring separate integration tests altogether.
